newsitem.title: ALBANIA: U.N. agency prepares aid distribution in Albania.
newsitem.headline: U.N. agency prepares aid distribution in Albania.

text.p: The U.N.'s World Food Programme (WFP) on Wednesday unloaded the first major shipment of emergency food aid in Albania since the arrival of an Italian-led security mission in the anarchic Balkan state.
A huge crane lifted hundreds of white sacks of wheat flour onto trucks which transported them to a warehouse at this sprawling Adriatic port, guarded by heavily armed French soldiers, witnesses said.

WFP, the world's biggest food aid agency, was unloading 360 tonnes of wheat flour and 36 tonnes of beans, brought by a Greek-owned ship, the Stavros Emmanuel, from the Italian port of Trieste. It said it hoped to begin deliveries on Friday.
"We have to unload everything today because we are scheduled to leave the port tomorrow," the ship's Greek captain Athanasios Konidaris told Reuters aboard the 554-tonne vessel.

Albania slid into near-anarchy last month after fraudulent investment schemes wiped out the savings of thousands of families. Nearly 300 people have been killed since people looted armouries deserted by soldiers and police.

The WFP shipment coincided with the arrival of some 1,200 Italian, French and Spanish troops as part of a 6,000-strong eight-nation mission to protect delivery of emergency food and medicines across the distressed country.

French armoured personnel carriers sped along the road between Durres and Tirana on Wednesday as Albanian police wearing black masks and armed with Kalashnikov rifles conducted spot checks on passing cars.

A French officer at Durres port, who asked not to be identified, said he was concerned about widespread banditry. He said troops had seen several suspicious transactions in the dock area involving the exchange of large sums of cash.

WFP said it would discuss plans for distributing the aid with the multinational force before sending out about 100 tonnes of wheat flour to destitute families in Elbasan, a central town 50 km (30 miles) southeast of the capital.
"We are planning to make our first distribution on Friday," Sasha Zarkovacki, the WFP's logistics officer, told Reuters at the port, 40 km (25 miles) west of Tirana.
WFP also planned to take 200 tonnes of relief to Kukes, a remote mountain town 208 km (125 miles) northeast of Tirana.
"We are hoping to have an escort from the multinational force, although we consider these areas to be relatively safe," Zarkovacki said.
He said there was no danger that the wheat flour and beans would perish as they could be stored for up to six months.
The aid agency was inviting state institutions, including hospitals and orphanages, to send vans to the Durres warehouse on Friday to take away some food, he added.
Albania's poor desperately need food. Basic food costs have shot up, social security payments have stopped and state food supplies are not reaching institutions, aid officials say.

Relief agencies estimate that one in 10 Albanians needs humanitarian aid. The Geneva-based International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), which does not rely on armed escorts, has been distributing food and medicines since last month.

The head of the WFP Albania mission, Jean-Marie Boucher, said on Tuesday the relief programme would last for a few months. "As this is not a famine, we are acting as a bridge until things return to normal," he said.
Another ship carrying 23 tonnes of vegetable oil was due to arrive from the southeastern Italian port of Brindisi within the next day or two, WFP said.
